title: Miksi: answering with koska
summary: Miksi asks why. Miksi sinä olet kotona? — Koska olen sairas.
prerequisiteSkills: Kuinka with an adjective: answering about degree
objectives: Give a reason beginning with koska, including a supplied negative reason.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
An adjective is a word that describes a quality.
Miksi asks why. Koska introduces the reason in the answer: Miksi olet kotona? — Koska olen sairas (“Why are you at home? — Because I am ill”).
keyPoints: Use miksi in the question and koska for the reason in the answer, not the reverse.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: A koska-clause is a natural short answer to miksi. Put koska before an ordinary statement with its person and verb. A full answer can repeat the main situation before the because-clause. Here the supporting clauses are provided, so the new decision is reason versus question.
A natural short reply to “Miksi sinä olet kotona?” is “Koska olen sairas.” (“Because I am ill.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.

After Miksi sinä et tule? (“Why aren't you coming?”), a reason can itself be negative: Koska en ole valmis (“Because I am not ready”). The complete question and negative phrase are given here; koska still introduces the reason.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.

A full reply can begin with the main statement: Olen kotona, koska olen sairas (“I am at home because I am ill”). Put a comma before koska. The short reply Koska olen sairas gives just the reason. Minä can be included with olen in either clause.
keyPoints: Begin the reason with koska rather than repeating the question word miksi.
